body.text: Kazakhstan is mourning the deaths of 14 servicemen who were lost during a military drill. The tragedy took place on September 24 during the 2026 Caspian Defense exercise in southwestern Kazakhstan. The episode has led to the dismissal of the defense minister, while five officials are being investigated for negligence in relation to the case.

According to the Kazakh Ministry of Defense, a total of 17 servicemen were swept out to sea during one of the naval exercises due to a sudden deterioration in weather in the area, including strong winds. While rescue teams did manage to save three servicemen, the remainder were lost, their bodies recovered over the following days.

While President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev declared a day of mourning out of respect for the soldiers who passed away, criticism has hit the authorities hard, both regarding the accident and the subsequent approach by the authorities to the relatives of the deceased.

The accidental deaths prompted criticism at all levels of authority, not least in regards to how the tragedy was communicated to the relatives who were left behind. As news about the September 24 accident spread, relatives of servicemen involved in the exercise started to gather outside the Aktau morgue located close to the scene of the accident. There they sought answers regarding who was lost, demanding the names of those who had been identified.

Separated by a fence surrounding the morgue, military personnel later that day read out the names of the identified servicemen, most of whom were under the age of 25. The scene, which was captured on video and shared on social media, quickly gained attention for its impersonal and monotonous tone, with both activists and journalists calling out the authorities for handling the announcement in a way that was “Shocking [and] heartless.”

In the week following the accident, disciplinary actions were rolled out, with five officials from the Ministry of Defense being detained and put under investigation for their role in the accident. Among those detained were the chief of staff working with the naval forces, two military unit commanders, and a naval infantry company commander connected to the incident. The men are allegedly to blame for the accident due to negligence of service and violation of navigation rules, according to Kazakh police.

The incident did also force consequences at the highest levels of governance. Initially, Tokayev gave his condolences to the affected families and declared a day of mourning, to be observed on September 25. Days later, he sacked the minister of defense, Dauren Kosanov, who had been in the post just over 15 months. In his place, the now former commander of special operation forces, Aidos Myrzakhmetov, was appointed.

This is not the first accident of its kind. Four servicemen died as strong winds hit a military exercise in the same area of southwestern Kazakhstan in 2015. While this time the investigation and reshuffling of people connected to the Ministry of Defense might help prevent the recurrence of such accidents, military analyst Yermek Seitbattalov, whom the outlet Kaztag spoke to, still sees multiple shortcomings that the military has not fixed. The retired colonel, among other things, mentioned flaws in combat training and the preparation of officers, specifically in relation to the safety of servicemen during exercises. He said this issue was one of the most important matters of attention for the new defense minister.

The Kazakh authorities have shown themselves unequipped not only to properly communicate the passing of soldiers to their loved ones, but also to ensure the safety of those participating in military exercises. While Kazakhstan still mourns the tragedy, the test will be what the military learns from it.
